contract:
EmailManager.getTransporter builds a nodemailer transport from Database.emailSettings.getTransportObject(). sendTest and sendEBookToDevice call transporter.verify() first (its own connection; a failed verify answers 400 'Failed to verify SMTP connection configuration' after logging the detail) and only then sendMail on a second connection, so an SMTP failure is never reported as a successful send. Envelope sender is the configured fromAddress; recipient is device.email for the ebook and testAddress || fromAddress for the test email. The ebook message has subject 'Here is your Ebook!', html '
' and one attachment {filename: ebookFile.metadata.filename, path: ebookFile.metadata.path}, serialized as multipart/mixed with a text/html part and a base64 application/epub+zip attachment. The test message has subject 'Test email from Audiobookshelf' and text 'Success!'. getTransportObject keeps secure only at port 465, forces secure false for every other port, adds auth only when user and pass are set, and adds tls.rejectUnauthorized false only when the setting is false.
exceptions: Implicit TLS on the IANA smtps port 465 cannot be exercised offline: binding a privileged port needs root. The 465 rule is asserted from the settings defaults and the transport object; TLS is exercised with STARTTLS on an unprivileged port.
The test and send routes share the transport code; their envelopes and MIME shapes are asserted by the route-r172 and route-r174 scenarios listed here.

invariants.contract: Both flows build one transport from the stored EmailSettings (host/port, tls only when rejectUnauthorized is false), call verify() on its own SMTP connection and only then call sendMail on a second connection. The ebook flow sends from fromAddress to the device email; the test flow sends to testAddress || fromAddress. verify() answers before any sendMail, and a message rejection is reported as a 400, never as OK.

The ebook message is multipart/mixed with one text/html part (body '
') and one base64 attachment whose Content-Type is derived from the ebook filename (application/epub+zip for .epub), whose filename is ebookFile.metadata.filename, and whose decoded bytes equal the file at ebookFile.metadata.path. The test message is a single text/plain; charset=utf-8 part with body 'Success!' and no attachment.

getTransportObject sends secure=true only when port is 465 and forces secure=false for other ports; it adds auth {user,pass} only when user is set and pass is defined; it sets tls.rejectUnauthorized=false only when the setting is false. With STARTTLS advertised, a trusted certificate upgrades both connections and delivers the message, while rejectUnauthorized true rejects the self-signed certificate with the fixed verification message. AUTH PLAIN carries exactly the configured user and password on the verification and delivery connections.

A verify failure answers 400 with 'Failed to verify SMTP connection configuration' and a sendMail-stage rejection answers 400, so neither route claims success; a client that cancels while SMTP never answers gets no success response and the server keeps serving requests.
